co-sb26-189.title: Colorado Senate Bill 26-189, Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Chapter 131 (automated decision-making technology in consequential decisions)

coveredParties.text: A developer is any Colorado business that creates or makes commercially available a covered ADMT.
coveredParties.quote: (8) (a) "DEVELOPER" MEANS A PERSON DOING BUSINESS IN COLORADO THAT: (I) DEVELOPS, OFFERS, SELLS, LEASES, LICENSES, OR OTHERWISE MAKES COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE A COVERED ADMT; (II) DEVELOPS A COMPONENT THAT IS DESIGNED, MARKETED, INTENDED, DOCUMENTED, ADVERTISED, CONFIGURED, OR CONTRACTED TO BE USED AS PART OF A COVERED ADMT; OR (III) INTENTIONALLY AND SUBSTANTIALLY MODIFIES AN ADMT SUCH THAT IT BECOMES A COVERED ADMT.

coveredParties.text: A deployer is any Colorado business that deploys a covered ADMT.
coveredParties.quote: (7) "DEPLOYER" MEANS A PERSON DOING BUSINESS IN COLORADO THAT DEPLOYS A COVERED ADMT.

coveredParties.text: Developers must keep compliance records for at least three years after record creation.
coveredParties.quote: A DEVELOPER SHALL RETAIN, FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER THE CREATION OF A RECORD REQUIRED OR CREATED UNDER THIS SECTION OR FOR A LONGER PERIOD IF REQUIRED BY APPLICABLE STATE OR FEDERAL LAW, RECORDS REASONABLY NECESSARY TO DEMONSTRATE COMPLIANCE WITH THIS SECTION.

coveredParties.text: Deployers must keep compliance records for at least three years after a consequential decision.
coveredParties.quote: A DEPLOYER SHALL RETAIN, FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER THE DATE OF A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION OR FOR A LONGER PERIOD IF REQUIRED BY APPLICABLE STATE OR FEDERAL LAW, RECORDS REASONABLY NECESSARY TO DEMONSTRATE COMPLIANCE WITH THIS PART 17.

coveredParties.text: Creditors must meet this law's notice requirements when federal notice satisfies them.
coveredParties.quote: A CREDITOR, WITH RESPECT TO A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION INVOLVING THE OFFERING, THE DENIAL, THE PRICING, THE SERVICING, OR OTHER MATERIAL TERMS OF CREDIT, THAT IS REQUIRED TO PROVIDE AND THAT PROVIDES A NOTICE TO A CONSUMER PURSUANT TO THE FEDERAL "EQUAL CREDIT OPPORTUNITY ACT", 15 U.S.C. SEC. 1691 ET SEQ., AND ITS IMPLEMENTING REGULATIONS, INCLUDING REGULATION B, 12 CFR 1002, AND, WHEN APPLICABLE, THE FEDERAL "FAIR CREDIT REPORTING ACT", 15 U.S.C. SEC. 1681 ET SEQ., COMPLIES WITH THE NOTICE OR DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION THAT RELATE TO THE SAME DECISION OR ADVERSE OUTCOME IF THE NOTICE PROVIDED TO THE CONSUMER PURSUANT TO THE FEDERAL LAWS AND REGULATIONS DESCRIBED IN THIS SUBSECTION (6)(a) ALSO SATISFIES THE NOTICE OR DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION.

coveredParties.text: Deployers or developers must give required notices and disclosures in an accessible way.
coveredParties.quote: (8) A DEPLOYER OR DEVELOPER SHALL PROVIDE THE NOTICES AND DISCLOSURES REQUIRED BY THIS PART 17 IN A MANNER THAT IS REASONABLY ACCESSIBLE TO CONSUMERS WITH DISABILITIES AND CONSUMERS WITH LIMITED ENGLISH PROFICIENCY, CONSISTENT WITH APPLICABLE STATE AND FEDERAL LAW.

coveredParties.text: Developers and deployers are the parties subject to the notice requirement.
coveredParties.quote: PRIOR TO ANY ENFORCEMENT ACTION FOR A VIOLATION OF THIS PART 17, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL ISSUE A NOTICE OF VIOLATION TO A DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER

coveredParties.text: Developers and deployers of covered ADMT are subject to liability.
coveredParties.quote: (1) A DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER MAY BE HELD LIABLE IN AN ACTION ALLEGING UNLAWFUL DISCRIMINATION UNDER STATE ANTI-DISCRIMINATION LAWS, INCLUDING THE "COLORADO ANTI-DISCRIMINATION ACT", PARTS 3 TO 8 OF ARTICLE 34 OF TITLE 24, ARISING FROM A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION MATERIALLY INFLUENCED BY A COVERED ADMT.

coveredParties.text: Insurers and affiliated entities are covered by this part.
coveredParties.quote: (1) (a) AN INSURER, AS DEFINED IN SECTION 10-1-102 (13), AND AFFILIATED ENTITIES THAT ARE SUBJECT TO THE REQUIREMENTS OF SECTION 10-3-1104.9 ARE IN COMPLIANCE WITH THIS PART 17 IN THE PRACTICE OF INSURANCE.

coveredParties.text: Covered health‑care entities must give patients a general notice about ADMT use.
coveredParties.quote: (c) A COVERED ENTITY SHALL PROVIDE PATIENTS WITH A GENERAL NOTICE OF USE OF ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES, INCLUDING A COVERED ADMT.

coveredParties.text: Covered entities using ADMT for patient eligibility decisions.
coveredParties.quote: A COVERED ENTITY THAT USES A COVERED ADMT TO DETERMINE A PATIENT'S ELIGIBILITY FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE, INCLUDING DISCOUNTED CARE AS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 25.5-3-502, SHALL PROVIDE A PATIENT THE FOLLOWING DISCLOSURES:

coveredParties.text: Deployers must follow federal law and give required disclosures.
coveredParties.quote: THE DEPLOYER SHALL COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE FEDERAL LAW AND PROVIDE DISCLOSURES AND ACCESS CONSISTENT WITH THAT LAW.

coveredParties.text: Any person who violates Part 17 commits a deceptive trade practice.
coveredParties.quote: (uuuu) VIOLATES PART 17 OF THIS ARTICLE 1.

triggers.text: The law applies when a covered ADMT is created or used to materially influence consequential decisions.
triggers.quote: (5) THIS SECTION APPLIES WHEN A DEVELOPER CREATES A COVERED ADMT THAT IS INTENDED, DOCUMENTED, MARKETED, ADVERTISED, CONFIGURED, OR CONTRACTED TO BE USED TO MAKE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISIONS OR WHEN THE DEVELOPER BECOMES AWARE THAT THE COVERED ADMT IS BEING USED TO MAKE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISIONS IN A MANNER CONSISTENT WITH THE INTENDED AND CONTRACTED USES.

triggers.text: Law applies when a developer creates or learns a covered ADMT used for consequential decisions.
triggers.quote: THIS SECTION APPLIES WHEN A DEVELOPER CREATES A COVERED ADMT THAT IS INTENDED, DOCUMENTED, MARKETED, ADVERTISED, CONFIGURED, OR CONTRACTED TO BE USED TO MAKE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISIONS OR WHEN THE DEVELOPER BECOMES AWARE THAT THE COVERED ADMT IS BEING USED TO MAKE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISIONS IN A MANNER CONSISTENT WITH THE INTENDED AND CONTRACTED USES.

triggers.text: Trigger: Deployers using covered ADMT that causes an adverse consumer outcome.
triggers.quote: IF A DEPLOYER USES A COVERED ADMT TO MATERIALLY INFLUENCE A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION THAT RESULTS IN AN ADVERSE OUTCOME FOR A CONSUMER, THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE WITHIN THIRTY DAYS AFTER MAKING THE DECISION:

triggers.text: Law applies when a consumer suffers adverse outcome from a consequential decision materially influenced by a covered ADMT.
triggers.quote: (1) (a) WHEN A CONSUMER EXPERIENCES AN ADVERSE OUTCOME RESULTING FROM A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION IN WHICH A COVERED ADMT MATERIALLY INFLUENCES THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION, THE CONSUMER MAY REQUEST...

triggers.text: A violation of Part 17 triggers the law's provisions.
triggers.quote: A VIOLATION OF THIS PART 17 IS A DECEPTIVE TRADE PRACTICE

triggers.text: Liability arises when a consequential decision is materially influenced by a covered ADMT.
triggers.quote: (1) A DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER MAY BE HELD LIABLE IN AN ACTION ALLEGING UNLAWFUL DISCRIMINATION ... ARISING FROM A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION MATERIALLY INFLUENCED BY A COVERED ADMT.

triggers.text: Insurers not in compliance must disclose their use of covered ADMT that influences insurance decisions.
triggers.quote: (1)(b) IF AN INSURER IS NOT DEEMED IN COMPLIANCE PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (1)(a) OF THIS SECTION, THE INSURER SHALL PROVIDE NOTICE AND DISCLOSURE OF ITS USE OF A COVERED ADMT IN MATERIALLY INFLUENCING A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION REGARDING THE PRACTICE OF INSURANCE PURSUANT TO THE DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS OF SECTION 6-1-1704 (3), TO THE EXTENT APPLICABLE.
triggers.failReason: quote not found in the law text

triggers.text: When a covered entity uses ADMT to decide patient eligibility for financial assistance, disclosures to the patient are triggered.
triggers.quote: (d) NOTWITHSTANDING SUBSECTION (3)(a) OF THIS SECTION, A COVERED ENTITY THAT USES A COVERED ADMT TO DETERMINE A PATIENT'S ELIGIBILITY FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE, INCLUDING DISCOUNTED CARE AS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 25.5-3-502, SHALL PROVIDE A PATIENT THE FOLLOWING DISCLOSURES:

triggers.text: Use of a covered ADMT to decide patient financial assistance eligibility.
triggers.quote: A COVERED ENTITY THAT USES A COVERED ADMT TO DETERMINE A PATIENT'S ELIGIBILITY FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE, INCLUDING DISCOUNTED CARE AS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 25.5-3-502, SHALL PROVIDE A PATIENT THE FOLLOWING DISCLOSURES:

triggers.text: Consequential decisions occurring on/after Jan 1 2027 trigger the law.
triggers.quote: This act applies to consequential decisions made on or after January 1, 2027.

obligations.text: Developers must provide deployers with comprehensive documentation about the ADMT, its uses, data, limitations, and compliance instructions.
obligations.quote: (1) ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, A DEVELOPER SHALL MAKE AVAILABLE TO EACH DEPLOYER OF A COVERED ADMT DEVELOPED BY THE DEVELOPER, IN A FORM AND MANNER THAT IS REASONABLY UNDERSTANDABLE TO A DEPLOYER AND THAT PROTECTS TRADE SECRETS OR INFORMATION PROTECTED FROM DISCLOSURE BY STATE OR FEDERAL LAW: (a) A GENERAL STATEMENT DESCRIBING THE INTENDED USES AND KNOWN HARMFUL OR INAPPROPRIATE USES OF THE COVERED ADMT; (b) A DESCRIPTION OF THE CATEGORIES OF DATA, INCLUDING PERSONAL DATA, USED TO TRAIN THE COVERED ADMT, TO THE EXTENT KNOWN; (c) KNOWN LIMITATIONS OF THE COVERED ADMT, INCLUDING KNOWN RISKS AND CIRCUMSTANCES IN WHICH THE COVERED ADMT SHOULD NOT BE USED; (d) INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE DEPLOYER'S APPROPRIATE USE, MONITORING, AND MEANINGFUL HUMAN REVIEW, WHERE APPLICABLE; (e) INFORMATION REASONABLY NECESSARY FOR THE DEPLOYER TO COMPLY WITH SECTION 6-1-1704. IF INFORMATION IS WITHHELD, THE DEVELOPER SHALL NOTIFY THE DEPLOYER.
obligations.timing: on or after January 1, 2027

obligations.text: Developers must notify deployers of material updates, modifications, or changes to use or risks within a reasonable time.
obligations.quote: (2) (a) A DEVELOPER SHALL PROVIDE TO EACH DEPLOYER OF A COVERED ADMT DEVELOPED BY THE DEVELOPER A NOTICE OF MATERIAL UPDATES, INTENTIONAL AND SUBSTANTIAL MODIFICATIONS, AND CHANGES TO THE INTENDED USE OF, LIMITATIONS FOR, OR RISK MITIGATION FOR THE COVERED ADMT WITHIN A REASONABLE TIME.
obligations.timing: within a reasonable time

obligations.text: Developers must keep compliance records for at least three years, or longer if law requires.
obligations.quote: (4) A DEVELOPER SHALL RETAIN, FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER THE CREATION OF A RECORD REQUIRED OR CREATED UNDER THIS SECTION OR FOR A LONGER PERIOD IF REQUIRED BY APPLICABLE STATE OR FEDERAL LAW, RECORDS REASONABLY NECESSARY TO DEMONSTRATE COMPLIANCE WITH THIS SECTION. RECORDS INCLUDE SYSTEM VERSION IDENTIFIERS, CHANGELOGS, AND DOCUMENTATION AND NOTICES OF MATERIAL UPDATES PROVIDED TO DEPLOYERS PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (2) OF THIS SECTION.
obligations.timing: for not less than three years after creation, or longer if required by law

obligations.text: Retain compliance records for at least three years after record creation.
obligations.quote: A DEVELOPER SHALL RETAIN, FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER THE CREATION OF A RECORD REQUIRED OR CREATED UNDER THIS SECTION OR FOR A LONGER PERIOD IF REQUIRED BY APPLICABLE STATE OR FEDERAL LAW, RECORDS REASONABLY NECESSARY TO DEMONSTRATE COMPLIANCE WITH THIS SECTION.
obligations.timing: FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER THE CREATION OF A RECORD

obligations.text: Retain compliance records for at least three years after a consequential decision.
obligations.quote: A DEPLOYER SHALL RETAIN, FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER THE DATE OF A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION OR FOR A LONGER PERIOD IF REQUIRED BY APPLICABLE STATE OR FEDERAL LAW, RECORDS REASONABLY NECESSARY TO DEMONSTRATE COMPLIANCE WITH THIS PART 17.
obligations.timing: FOR NOT LESS THAN THREE YEARS AFTER THE DATE OF A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION

obligations.text: Give clear notice to consumers before using covered ADMT to influence a consequential decision.
obligations.quote: PRIOR TO A DEPLOYER USING A COVERED ADMT TO MATERIALLY INFLUENCE A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION, THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE A CLEAR AND CONSPICUOUS NOTICE TO A CONSUMER THAT THE DEPLOYER USED OR WILL USE A COVERED ADMT IN A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION AFFECTING THE CONSUMER AND INSTRUCTIONS REGARDING HOW THE CONSUMER MAY OBTAIN THE ADDITIONAL INFORMATION DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION.
obligations.timing: PRIOR TO A DEPLOYER USING A COVERED ADMT

obligations.text: Maintain a prominent public notice accessible at consumer interaction points.
obligations.quote: A DEPLOYER COMPLIES WITH SUBSECTION (1) OF THIS SECTION BY MAINTAINING A PROMINENT PUBLIC NOTICE THAT IS REASONABLY ACCESSIBLE AT POINTS OF CONSUMER INTERACTION, INCLUDING THROUGH A LINK OR POSTING THAT IS REASONABLY PROXIMATE TO THE INTERACTION OR TRANSACTION IN WHICH A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION MAY OCCUR.

obligations.text: After an adverse outcome, provide required disclosures within 30 days of the decision.
obligations.quote: IF A DEPLOYER USES A COVERED ADMT TO MATERIALLY INFLUENCE A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION THAT RESULTS IN AN ADVERSE OUTCOME FOR A CONSUMER, THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE WITHIN THIRTY DAYS AFTER MAKING THE DECISION: (a) A PLAIN LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION OF THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION AND THE ROLE THE COVERED ADMT PLAYED IN THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION; (b) INSTRUCTIONS AND A SIMPLE-TO-FOLLOW PROCESS TO REQUEST ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE COVERED ADMT AND THE INPUTS, INCLUDING THE NAME OF THE COVERED ADMT, THE COVERED ADMT VERSION NUMBER, IF APPLICABLE, THE COVERED ADMT DEVELOPER, AND THE TYPES, CATEGORIES, AND SOURCES OF PERSONAL DATA USED, TO THE EXTENT THE DEPLOYER RECEIVES THE NECESSARY INFORMATION FROM THE DEVELOPER IN COMPLIANCE WITH SECTION 6-1-1702; AND (c) AN EXPLANATION OF THE CONSUMER RIGHTS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 6-1-1705 AND HOW TO EXERCISE THEM.
obligations.timing: WITHIN THIRTY DAYS AFTER MAKING THE DECISION

obligations.text: Adopt rules clarifying post‑adverse‑outcome disclosure requirements by Jan 1 2027.
obligations.quote: ON OR BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2027, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL ADOPT RULES TO CLARIFY AND IMPLEMENT THE POST-ADVERSE OUTCOME DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS SET FORTH IN SUBSECTION (3) OF THIS SECTION.
obligations.timing: ON OR BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2027

obligations.text: Notify the consumer when withholding trade‑secret or protected information.
obligations.quote: IF A DEPLOYER WITHHOLDS INFORMATION PURSUANT TO THIS SUBSECTION (5), THE DEPLOYER SHALL NOTIFY THE CONSUMER.

obligations.text: Creditors must meet this law's notice requirements when federal notice satisfies them.
obligations.quote: A CREDITOR, WITH RESPECT TO A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION INVOLVING THE OFFERING, THE DENIAL, THE PRICING, THE SERVICING, OR OTHER MATERIAL TERMS OF CREDIT, THAT IS REQUIRED TO PROVIDE AND THAT PROVIDES A NOTICE TO A CONSUMER PURSUANT TO THE FEDERAL "EQUAL CREDIT OPPORTUNITY ACT", 15 U.S.C. SEC. 1691 ET SEQ., AND ITS IMPLEMENTING REGULATIONS, INCLUDING REGULATION B, 12 CFR 1002, AND, WHEN APPLICABLE, THE FEDERAL "FAIR CREDIT REPORTING ACT", 15 U.S.C. SEC. 1681 ET SEQ., COMPLIES WITH THE NOTICE OR DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION THAT RELATE TO THE SAME DECISION OR ADVERSE OUTCOME IF THE NOTICE PROVIDED TO THE CONSUMER PURSUANT TO THE FEDERAL LAWS AND REGULATIONS DESCRIBED IN THIS SUBSECTION (6)(a) ALSO SATISFIES THE NOTICE OR DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION.

obligations.text: Provide required notices in an accessible format for disabled and limited‑English‑proficiency consumers.
obligations.quote: A DEPLOYER OR DEVELOPER SHALL PROVIDE THE NOTICES AND DISCLOSURES REQUIRED BY THIS PART 17 IN A MANNER THAT IS REASONABLY ACCESSIBLE TO CONSUMERS WITH DISABILITIES AND CONSUMERS WITH LIMITED ENGLISH PROFICIENCY, CONSISTENT WITH APPLICABLE STATE AND FEDERAL LAW.

obligations.text: Provide required notices and disclosures in a manner reasonably accessible to disabled and limited‑English‑proficiency consumers.
obligations.quote: (8) A DEPLOYER OR DEVELOPER SHALL PROVIDE THE NOTICES AND DISCLOSURES REQUIRED BY THIS PART 17 IN A MANNER THAT IS REASONABLY ACCESSIBLE TO CONSUMERS WITH DISABILITIES AND CONSUMERS WITH LIMITED ENGLISH PROFICIENCY, CONSISTENT WITH APPLICABLE STATE AND FEDERAL LAW.

obligations.text: For education decisions, a FERPA‑covered deployer meets notice requirements using FERPA‑consistent processes.
obligations.quote: (9) (a) FOR A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION RELATING TO EDUCATION, A DEPLOYER THAT IS SUBJECT TO FERPA SATISFIES THE NOTICE AND DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION BY PROVIDING NOTICE AND DISCLOSURES THROUGH PROCESSES AND CHANNELS THAT ARE CONSISTENT WITH FERPA AND THE DEPLOYER'S FERPA NOTICES AND STUDENT RECORD ACCESS PROCEDURES, INCLUDING, WHERE APPLICABLE, NOTICE TO A PARENT OR GUARDIAN OR AN ELIGIBLE STUDENT.

obligations.text: Upon consumer request, provide data‑correction instructions and an opportunity for meaningful human review.
obligations.quote: (1) (a) WHEN A CONSUMER EXPERIENCES AN ADVERSE OUTCOME RESULTING FROM A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION IN WHICH A COVERED ADMT MATERIALLY INFLUENCES THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION, THE CONSUMER MAY REQUEST AND THE DEPLOYER SHALL PROVIDE IN RESPONSE TO THE REQUEST: (I) INSTRUCTIONS FOR REQUESTING PERSONAL DATA AND CORRECTING FACTUALLY INCORRECT OR MATERIALLY INACCURATE PERSONAL DATA USED IN A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION THAT USED A COVERED ADMT CONSISTENT WITH SECTION 6-1-1306; (II) AN OPPORTUNITY FOR MEANINGFUL HUMAN REVIEW AND RECONSIDERATION OF THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION, TO THE EXTENT COMMERCIALLY REASONABLE.
obligations.failReason: quote not found in the law text

obligations.text: FERPA‑covered deployers must use existing student‑record procedures to allow correction requests and reconsideration.
obligations.quote: (2) (a) FOR A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION RELATING TO EDUCATION, A DEPLOYER THAT IS SUBJECT TO FERPA COMPLIES WITH THE REQUIREMENTS OF SUBSECTION (1) OF THIS SECTION THROUGH THE DEPLOYER'S EXISTING STUDENT RECORD INSPECTION, REVIEW, AND AMENDMENT PROCEDURES AND ANY APPLICABLE DISTRICT COMPLAINT OR APPEAL PROCESS, IF THE DEPLOYER OFFERS A REASONABLE MECHANISM FOR A PARENT, GUARDIAN, OR ELIGIBLE STUDENT TO REQUEST CORRECTION OF MATERIALLY INACCURATE PERSONAL DATA AND RECONSIDERATION WHERE APPLICABLE UNDER THIS PART 17.

obligations.text: Adopt clarifying rules for this part by January 1 2027.
obligations.quote: (3) ON OR BEFORE JANUARY 1, 2027, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL ADOPT RULES TO CLARIFY AND IMPLEMENT THE REQUIREMENTS OF THIS SECTION.
obligations.timing: On or before January 1, 2027

obligations.text: Attorney General must issue a notice of violation before any enforcement action.
obligations.quote: PRIOR TO ANY ENFORCEMENT ACTION FOR A VIOLATION OF THIS PART 17, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL ISSUE A NOTICE OF VIOLATION TO A DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER
obligations.timing: PRIOR TO ANY ENFORCEMENT ACTION

obligations.text: Developer or deployer must cure the violation within 60 days after receiving notice.
obligations.quote: (b) IF THE DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER FAILS TO CURE A VIOLATION WITHIN SIXTY DAYS AFTER RECEIPT OF A NOTICE OF VIOLATION, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL MAY BRING AN ACTION PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION.
obligations.timing: WITHIN SIXTY DAYS AFTER RECEIPT OF A NOTICE OF VIOLATION

obligations.text: Attorney General must submit an annual enforcement report each January starting in 2028.
obligations.quote: (e) BEGINNING IN JANUARY 2028, AND IN JANUARY EVERY YEAR THEREAFTER, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL INCLUDE, AS PART OF THE DEPARTMENT OF LAW'S PRESENTATION DURING ITS "SMART ACT" HEARING REQUIRED BY SECTION 2-7-203, A REPORT CONCERNING ENFORCEMENT ACTIONS BROUGHT AND CURE PERIODS OFFERED BY THE ATTORNEY GENERAL RELATED TO VIOLATIONS OF THIS PART 17, INCLUDING:
obligations.timing: BEGINNING IN JANUARY 2028, AND IN JANUARY EVERY YEAR THEREAFTER

obligations.text: Attorney General must use a stakeholder engagement process when adopting rules.
obligations.quote: (c) IN ADOPTING RULES PURSUANT TO THIS PART 17, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL UTILIZE A PROCESS THAT MEANINGFULLY ENGAGES STAKEHOLDERS, INCLUDING CONSUMER ADVOCATES, DEPLOYERS, DEVELOPERS, AND SECTOR REGULATORS, THROUGH PUBLIC NOTICE, OPPORTUNITY FOR WRITTEN COMMENT, AND AT LEAST ONE PUBLIC HEARING AND SHALL ADOPT RULES IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 24-4-103.

obligations.text: Contracts may not contain indemnity clauses that shield parties from liability under this section.
obligations.quote: (7) (a) NOTWITHSTANDING ANY OTHER PROVISION OF LAW, IF A PROVISION OF A CONTRACT FOR THE USE OF AUTOMATED DECISION-MAKING TECHNOLOGY IN MAKING A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION OR ANY OTHER CONTRACT BETWEEN A DEVELOPER AND DEPLOYER PURPORTS TO INDEMNIFY, DEFEND, OR HOLD HARMLESS OR HAS THE EFFECT OF INDEMNIFYING, DEFENDING, OR HOLDING HARMLESS THE INDEMNITEE FROM OR AGAINST ANY LIABILITY FOR DAMAGES PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION RESULTING FROM THE DEVELOPER'S OR DEPLOYER'S OWN ACTS OR OMISSIONS RELATED TO THE USE OF AUTOMATED DECISION-MAKING TECHNOLOGY IN MAKING CONSEQUENTIAL DECISIONS IN VIOLATION OF THE "COLORADO ANTI-DISCRIMINATION ACT", PARTS 3 TO 8 OF ARTICLE 34 OF TITLE 24, OR OTHER COLORADO ANTI-DISCRIMINATION LAW, THE PROVISION IS CONTRARY TO PUBLIC POLICY AND VOID.

obligations.text: Non‑compliant insurers must disclose their use of covered ADMT that influences insurance decisions.
obligations.quote: (1)(b) IF AN INSURER IS NOT DEEMED IN COMPLIANCE PURSUANT TO SUBSECTION (1)(a) OF THIS SECTION, THE INSURER SHALL PROVIDE NOTICE AND DISCLOSURE OF ITS USE OF A COVERED ADMT IN MATERIALLY INFLUENCING A CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION REGARDING THE PRACTICE OF INSURANCE PURSUANT TO THE DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS OF SECTION 6-1-1704 (3), TO THE EXTENT APPLICABLE.
obligations.failReason: quote not found in the law text

obligations.text: Covered entities must give patients a general notice about use of covered ADMT.
obligations.quote: (c) A COVERED ENTITY SHALL PROVIDE PATIENTS WITH A GENERAL NOTICE OF USE OF ADVANCED TECHNOLOGIES, INCLUDING A COVERED ADMT.

obligations.text: Covered entities must provide specific disclosures when ADMT determines patient eligibility for financial assistance.
obligations.quote: (d) NOTWITHSTANDING SUBSECTION (3)(a) OF THIS SECTION, A COVERED ENTITY THAT USES A COVERED ADMT TO DETERMINE A PATIENT'S ELIGIBILITY FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE, INCLUDING DISCOUNTED CARE AS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 25.5-3-502, SHALL PROVIDE A PATIENT THE FOLLOWING DISCLOSURES:

obligations.text: Provide patients four disclosures about the decision, data used, correction process, and request for human review.
obligations.quote: A COVERED ENTITY THAT USES A COVERED ADMT TO DETERMINE A PATIENT'S ELIGIBILITY FOR FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE, INCLUDING DISCOUNTED CARE AS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 25.5-3-502, SHALL PROVIDE A PATIENT THE FOLLOWING DISCLOSURES: (I) A PLAIN LANGUAGE DESCRIPTION OF THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION AND THE ROLE OF THE COVERED ADMT IN THE CONSEQUENTIAL DECISION; (II) THE TYPES OF INFORMATION ABOUT THE INDIVIDUAL THE COVERED ENTITY RELIED UPON IN MAKING ITS DETERMINATION OF ELIGIBILITY, EXCEPT FOR TRADE SECRETS AND OTHER CONFIDENTIAL OR LEGALLY PROTECTED INFORMATION; (III) INFORMATION ON HOW TO REQUEST CORRECTION OF MATERIALLY INACCURATE PERSONAL DATA HELD BY THE COVERED ENTITY CONSISTENT WITH THE FEDERAL "HEALTH INSURANCE PORTABILITY AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT OF 1996", 42 U.S.C. SECS. 1320d TO 1320d-9 AND SECTION 25.5-3-502; AND (IV) INFORMATION ON HOW TO REQUEST MEANINGFUL HUMAN REVIEW OR RECONSIDERATION, WHERE APPLICABLE.

obligations.text: Give the required disclosures either in advance or within 30 days after an adverse outcome.
obligations.quote: A COVERED ENTITY MAY COMPLY WITH SUBSECTION (3)(d) OF THIS SECTION THROUGH EITHER AN ADVANCE GENERAL DISCLOSURE OF THE INFORMATION REQUIRED BY SUBSECTION (3)(d) OF THIS SECTION OR THROUGH A NOTICE PROVIDED WITHIN THIRTY CALENDAR DAYS AFTER AN ADVERSE OUTCOME.
obligations.timing: within thirty calendar days after an adverse outcome

obligations.text: Deployers must follow federal law and give required disclosures.
obligations.quote: THE DEPLOYER SHALL COMPLY WITH APPLICABLE FEDERAL LAW AND PROVIDE DISCLOSURES AND ACCESS CONSISTENT WITH THAT LAW.

penalties.text: Violations are enforceable only by the Attorney General.
penalties.quote: (b) VIOLATIONS OF THE DISCLOSURE REQUIREMENTS AND CONSUMER RIGHTS DESCRIBED IN SECTIONS 6-1-1702, 6-1-1703, 6-1-1704, AND 6-1-1705 ARE ENFORCEABLE EXCLUSIVELY BY THE ATTORNEY GENERAL WITHOUT REGARD TO ANY OTHER PROVISION IN THIS TITLE 6.

penalties.text: Violations constitute a deceptive trade practice under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act.
penalties.quote: (2) (a) A VIOLATION OF THIS PART 17 IS A DECEPTIVE TRADE PRACTICE AND IS SUBJECT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE "COLORADO CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT", THIS ARTICLE 1.

enforcedBy.text: Attorney General enforces Part 17 under the Colorado Consumer Protection Act.
enforcedBy.quote: (1) (a) THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL ENFORCE THIS PART 17 THROUGH THE "COLORADO CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT", THIS ARTICLE 1.

enforcedBy.text: Attorney General has exclusive enforcement authority for violations of Part 17.
enforcedBy.quote: (b) ANY PROVISION OF THE "COLORADO CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT", THIS ARTICLE 1, THAT IS INCONSISTENT WITH THE EXCLUSIVE ENFORCEMENT AUTHORITY GRANTED TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL IN THIS SECTION FOR A VIOLATION OF THIS PART 17 DOES NOT APPLY TO ANY SUCH VIOLATION.

enforcedBy.text: Attorney General enforces the part by adopting rules after stakeholder process.
enforcedBy.quote: (c) IN ADOPTING RULES PURSUANT TO THIS PART 17, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL SHALL UTILIZE A PROCESS THAT MEANINGFULLY ENGAGES STAKEHOLDERS, INCLUDING CONSUMER ADVOCATES, DEPLOYERS, DEVELOPERS, AND SECTOR REGULATORS, THROUGH PUBLIC NOTICE, OPPORTUNITY FOR WRITTEN COMMENT, AND AT LEAST ONE PUBLIC HEARING AND SHALL ADOPT RULES IN ACCORDANCE WITH SECTION 24-4-103.

curePeriod.text: Cure period is 60 days after receipt of a notice of violation.
curePeriod.quote: (b) IF THE DEVELOPER OR DEPLOYER FAILS TO CURE A VIOLATION WITHIN SIXTY DAYS AFTER RECEIPT OF A NOTICE OF VIOLATION, THE ATTORNEY GENERAL MAY BRING AN ACTION PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION.

effectiveDate.text: Developer documentation obligations begin on January 1, 2027.
